evidence: gitutil.py run_git_bounded: `invoke = run_git if runner is None else runner` — the branch under test
sync.py:70 `return run_git_bounded(tracker, *args, timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT, runner=run_git)` with docstring 'handed THIS module's run_git so the tests that patch sync.run_git by name keep intercepting'
tests/unit/test_store.py:167-172 patches `mod.subprocess.run` (shared by both paths), not `run_git`, so it cannot distinguish runner-used from runner-ignored
tests/unit/test_read_freshness_parity.py:135-140 _FetchSpy only intercepts `args[0]=='fetch'`, and sync fetch does not go through _git/run_git_bounded

ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit/store/test_git_outcome.py or elsewhere drives a TimeoutExpired through sync._git/push._git while patching that module's `run_git` by name to assert the passed runner was invoked (search 'run_git_bounded' and 'runner=' in tests returned no matches)
advisory.finding: The newly-introduced `runner` parameter of gitutil.run_git_bounded — the whole point of which is that push._git/sync._git hand in their own late-bound run_git so a test patching `<module>.run_git` by name still intercepts — has no test that would fail if run_git_bounded ignored `runner` and always used gitutil.run_git. The existing timeout tests patch subprocess.run (a seam both code paths share), and test_read_freshness_parity's fetch spy does not route through _git/run_git_bounded, so the seam-preservation contract the diff explicitly adds is regression-blind.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_git_outcome.py add a test that monkeypatches `sync.run_git` with a spy raising subprocess.TimeoutExpired, calls sync._git, and asserts (a) returncode==124 and (b) the spy was called — so ignoring the `runner` argument (falling back to gitutil.run_git) would make the spy record zero calls and fail.
